co2.guideText:
Sustainability and LCA (Life Cycle Assessment)

Choosing the right piping system has a significant impact on the carbon footprint of a building or industrial facility. The K-Aqua CO2 calculator enables a comprehensive Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) in accordance with EN 15804 standards. This analysis covers the entire lifecycle: from raw material extraction and product manufacturing (phases A1-A3), to transport and installation (phases A4-A5), right through to the operational phase (phase B) and end-of-life (phase C).

Compared to conventional metal pipes made of copper or steel, K-Aqua's PP-R and PPRCT pipes boast a significantly superior environmental footprint. The lower energy required for plastic extrusion, along with its considerably lighter weight, drastically reduces CO2 emissions during production and transport. Furthermore, the mirror-smooth inner surface (roughness of just 0.007 mm) ensures extremely low flow resistance. According to the Darcy-Weisbach equation, this means that circulation pumps require significantly less energy (electricity) to move fluid through the system.

Particularly during the operational phase (phase B), which for piping systems often lasts 50 years or longer, this energy conservation adds up to massive CO2 and cost savings (Total Cost of Ownership, TCO). Polypropylene also offers ecological advantages at the end of its life (phase C), as it is 100% recyclable and can be repurposed in the spirit of the circular economy (module D). Use this calculator to precisely and transparently quantify the ecological and economic savings potential of your K-Aqua project.

manifesto.title: The Architecture of Infallibility.
manifesto.lead: A piping system is the cardiovascular system of every mega-project. A failure means an infrastructural heart attack. That's why we don't speak of pipes, but of vital industrial arteries. Every term in this glossary represents a pillar of our zero-defect philosophy.

scroll.title: The K Aqua Process.
scroll.lead: From the molecular granule level to the final pressure test. Understand the physical principles that make our systems indestructible.

items.title: High-Pressure Extrusion Dynamics
items.desc: The thermoplastic deformation in our factories is subject to precise temperature control within 0.1 °C. This crystalline perfection guarantees a flawless, homogeneous molecular structure that absolutely precludes microscopic crack formation (stress cracking) even under extreme pressure and temperature fluctuations. When the material leaves our extruder, it is no longer a simple plastic. It is an industrial monolith.

items.title: Hydrostatic Stress Tests
items.desc: In our test laboratories, every pipe is subjected to a hydrostatic simulation that far exceeds real-world conditions. We apply internal pressures that lie beyond any normative requirement (up to 100 bar, depending on the SDR class). This ensures the integrity of the weld seams and the molecular elasticity of the PP-R material over a projected lifespan of more than 50 years in critical infrastructures.

items.title: Polyfusion Welding Technology
items.desc: Connections are the weak point in conventional systems. K Aqua eliminates this risk through polyfusion. At the molecular level, pipe and fitting merge into an inseparable, continuous unit. There are no threads to corrode, no seals to fail. The result is a piping system that behaves as if it were cast from a single piece.

items.title: Cavitation Resistance & Fluid Mechanics
items.desc: With an ultra-smooth inner wall (roughness < 0.007 mm), K Aqua pipes minimise flow resistance to nearly zero. This prevents the formation of biofilms and eliminates micro-cavitational effects at high-velocity flows. Pressure losses in the system are drastically reduced, maximising the energy efficiency of connected pump systems on an industrial scale.

bento.title: Technical Parameters.
bento.lead: The most important vocabulary of industrial piping technology, distilled to its essence.

items.title: PP-R (Polypropylene Random Copolymer)
items.desc: The molecular basis. A highly crystalline thermoplastic polymer that offers exceptional resistance to high temperatures and pressures. It is the DNA of our longevity.

items.title: Linear Thermal Expansion
items.desc: The change in length of the material during temperature changes. Our fibre-reinforced (Faser) pipes reduce this value to an absolute minimum (α = 0.035 mm/mK), which enormously increases structural stability in shafts.

items.title: Creep Rupture Strength
items.desc: The ability of the system to withstand constant internal pressure at specific temperatures over decades without deforming or bursting. K Aqua pipes are calibrated for 50+ years.

items.title: Pressure Loss Coefficient
items.desc: A mathematical value that describes the energy loss of the flow due to friction on the inner pipe wall. Through nano-smooth surfaces, this value is marginalised in K Aqua systems.

items.title: SDR (Standard Dimension Ratio)
items.desc: The ratio between the outer diameter (d) and the wall thickness (s). An SDR 6 pipe withstands massively higher pressures than an SDR 11 pipe. The correct choice is crucial for system design.

conclusion.title: Resistance to degradation in extreme cases.
conclusion.p1: In industrial applications, it is not normal operation that decides the quality of a piping system, but its stability in borderline areas. Chemical corrosion, cavitation from pressure surges, and thermal shocks are the natural enemies of conventional installations.
conclusion.p2: The K Aqua Matrix isolates the fluid medium from the environment through an inert barrier layer. No ion exchange takes place. Metallic systems degrade from the moment water flows through them. They sacrifice themselves to function. Our PP-R system remains immaculate on the inside even after decades.
conclusion.p3: The concept of Environmental Stress Cracking Resistance (ESCR) is of central importance in polymer chemistry. We modify the molecular weight of our copolymer so that it cushions peak loads instead of breaking under them. The result is a system that absorbs shocks, vibrations, and structural settlements.
conclusion.p4: Anyone who has understood the terminology of piping technology also understands why compromises here can mean ruin. German Engineering is not an empty promise, but the sum of precise, physical parameters that we manifest in every single centimetre of our production.

faq.q: What media is the system designed for?
faq.a: For drinking water (hot and cold) with high temperature and pressure resistance over decades. Because PP is resistant to solvents, alkalis, and acids, industrial applications are also possible; we test these with you on a project-specific basis.

faq.q: What do the five SDR classes stand for?
faq.a: SDR is the Standard Dimension Ratio (outer diameter divided by wall thickness, d/s). Smaller SDR = thicker wall = higher nominal pressure: SDR 6 equates to PN 20, SDR 17 equates to PN 6. This lets you choose the exact reserve you need for each application, without over-dimensioning.

faq.q: When to use Monolayer, and when K-Fiber?
faq.a: Monolayer is the economical standard for most applications. The glass fibre reinforced composite reduces thermal expansion to about a quarter, allows for larger bracket spacing, and remains dimensionally stable for large dimensions and hot water—the choice for risers, circulation, and d ≥ 160.

Materially bonded by welding: manual socket welding (up to d63) or machine, electrofusion via electrofusion fittings, and butt welding for large dimensions up to d630. The corresponding devices and tools are part of the range; the Academy videos demonstrate all four methods.

faq.q: Is the system compliant with drinking water standards?
faq.a: The system is developed for drinking water; polypropylene is taste and odour neutral. We provide the certificates of conformity for drinking water contact (DVGW/KTW) in the Trust Centre as part of the RFP document package.

faq.q: What lifespan is the design based on?

procs.t: Manual socket welding: up to d63

steps.d: Cut the pipe at a right angle, deburr cleanly, and chamfer. Use pipe cutters from the K Aqua tool range.
Mark the insertion depth according to the table (e.g. 14 mm for d20) on the pipe: this defines the joining zone.
Push the pipe into the heating bush, fitting onto the heating spigot. Push on simultaneously and precisely hold the heating time.
Join axially within the changeover time. Never twist: twisting destroys the plasticised structure.
Hold the connection fixed for a few seconds, then wait out the cooling time before applying mechanical load.
Cut, deburr, mark welding depth. The basic rules remain identical.
The machine holds both joining partners coaxially. Misalignment and tilting errors are mechanically excluded.
Heating bush and spigot according to DVS guidelines; the machine maintains position and time reproducibly.
The feed joins axially and evenly, particularly key to consistent quality from d75 to d125.
Only unclamp and continue processing after the cooling time has elapsed.
Peel and clean the pipe surface in the joining zone. Oxide skin and dirt prevent welding.
Mark the depth on the pipe, push the pipe into the fitting up to the stop.
Use retaining clamps: the fitting must not be under bending stress during welding.
The device supplies power to the embedded heating coils in the fitting. Parameters come from the fitting, not from feeling.
Only move or load after the specified cooling time. Check control indicators on the fitting.

procs.t: Butt Fusion: Large dimensions up to d630

steps.d: Plane both pipe ends in the machine until continuous shavings form: plane parallelism is mandatory.
Maximum offset is 10% of the wall thickness. At d630, every millimetre counts.
Equalise under pressure until bead formation, then heat through without pressure. Times according to DVS 2207-11.
Remove the heating element swiftly and bring the ends together under defined joining pressure.
The joining pressure remains until the end of the cooling time, then the homogeneous, permanently tight pipeline is formed.

gloss: Standard Dimension Ratio = Outer diameter divided by wall thickness (d/s). Smaller SDR = thicker wall = higher nominal pressure.
Nominal Pressure (Pressure Nominal). An older classification for the pressure rating (e.g. PN20), increasingly being replaced by SDR.
Polypropylene Random Copolymer with modified crystalline structure. Higher pressure resistance at high temperatures compared to standard PP-R.
Stumpfschweißen. The ends of pipes/fittings of the same diameter and wall thickness are heated and pressed against each other.
Elektroschweißen. Welding using fittings with embedded heating coils, activated by a welding device.
Umstellzeit. The maximum allowed time between removing the heating element and joining the parts.
